text:
maria: Quick Q — documenting routing behavior for /v1/generate. If a client sends model_hint: "gpt-std" and region_tier: "eu-standard", but that exact model variant isn't available in eu, what should the API do by default? fall back to nearest region, pick lower tier, or return an error? I'm writing a compatibility note for the SDKs.

aj: Short answer: prefer region match first, then compatible variant, then tier, then cross-region. Routing order we use today: 1) exact variant in requested region, 2) compatible variant in same region, 3) same variant in other region (respecting customer routing_policy), 4) compatible lower-tier variant. For Dedicated customers we honor pinning.

noah: Tiny nuance to call out — if a Dedicated/Private tenant has pinned model_version, we do NOT cross-region fallback. Current runtime surface returns 412 with error code "model_unavailable" and payload includes "can_fallback": false. Do we want docs to mandate that behavior or change it to return 409 + suggestion?

sara: For hosted customers we allow cross-region fallback when routing_policy=="default". For strict routing_policy=="region_only" we return 412. I can add explicit examples in the doc.

maria: Cool. Example payload I'm planning to show in examples: 
```json
{ "model_hint": "gpt-std", "region_tier": "eu-standard", "routing_policy": "default" }
```
If fallback happens, should the canonical response be 200 with an added routing object (selected_model + fallback_chain + reason), or should we return a 206/redirect-like status? I want something consistent for SDKs.

aj: We added a "routing" object in v2 responses last month. Canonical example we discussed internally: 
```json
"routing": {
  "selected_model": "gpt-std-1.2-eu",
  "fallback_chain": ["gpt-std-1.2-eu","gpt-std-1.2-us","gpt-compact-1.0-us"],
  "reason": "region_unavailable"
}
```
Return 200 for successful generation with routing metadata. For strict failures (no fallback allowed) we keep 412/"model_unavailable". We were debating whether to make the full fallback_chain always present or opt-in.

noah: Perf note — full fallback_chain in every response can increase payload size and affects streaming overhead. Suggest capping fallback_chain length to 3 and making detailed chain opt-in via a header or query flag (e.g., Accept-Routing: full|minimal or ?routing_debug=true). Default should be minimal: selected_model + reason.

deploy-bot: @maria docs patch 0b3f2 queued for merge to staging :white_check_mark:

sara: Action: I'll update the docs to call out Dedicated pinning behavior, the 412 semantics, and add the example response with both minimal and full routing formats. @aj can you confirm whether we like header toggle or query param for debug?

aj: I prefer a header (Accept-Routing: full|minimal) to avoid changing URL surfaces and caching semantics. I'll open a tiny PR to add header handling and tests. Pinging @noah for review.

maria: Great. I'll also document that old param "model_alias" is deprecated — clients should send model_hint + optional model_version. For legacy clients we will keep returning 412 but include "suggested_models" in the error body for a year.

sara: ack, thanks all. I'll link the PR into the docs PR when ready.

maria: Final checklist for docs PR: 1) routing order table, 2) example request/response (minimal + full), 3) Dedicated/Private pinning note, 4) deprecation note for model_alias, 5) mention Accept-Routing header. I'll send the PR after @aj's header PR lands. :+1:
